I have farmed this land for over 30 years. My father farmed it before me. We are in the North China Plain — the soil is good loam, and we have a deep well for irrigation. There is really no question in my mind what I will grow. Everyone here grows winter wheat, then summer maize on the same land. That is two harvests a year. That is how I make my income.

I have about 10 mu. I will plant all of it in wheat in October, harvest in June, then immediately plant maize. Same land, two crops. That is the only way to make the land pay.

For wheat I will use an improved variety — something like 衡麦 or whatever the seed station nearby is selling this year. Not traditional seed — nobody uses that anymore, the yields are too low. I will irrigate four times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain fill. The soil here dries out. I will put down plenty of nitrogen — base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress at jointing. I spray herbicide in spring and something for aphids closer to heading. I use rotary tillage before wheat — it breaks up the compacted layer after corn.

For maize I will plant a hybrid, probably 郑单958 or 先玉335. After the wheat I just direct-seed into the stubble — no-tillage, saves time, the soil is already loose enough in summer. Rain usually comes July and August so I only irrigate once or twice. I put nitrogen down in two splits. One pesticide spray for fall armyworm, maybe a second if it gets bad.

I am not going to change what has worked for 30 years. Prices were decent last year. I will plant the same.
